prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an outdoor paved yard where a large wheeled metal rack containing stacked blue trays stands 0.3–2.5 m directly in front of and to the right of the camera wearer across the five frames, with a sloping ground gradient receding into a dark background beyond 5 m. In frames 2 and 4, the wearer's extended left hand and forearm appear brightest in the lower foreground at 0.3–0.5 m (within arm's reach of the nearest rack bars), while a person in black stands 2–2.5 m ahead to the left in frame 2 (within arm's reach of the rack's far corner) and approaches to 0.8–1.2 m at the left edge of frames 3 and 4 as the wearer turns slightly left and then right in frame 5, where another person stands about 3 m away beside the rack's right T-bar handle. A crouching person in red behind the rack (~3 m away) is occluded by the metal grid, and the person in black is partly out of view at the top and left frame borders in frames 2–4. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the near vertical struts of the rack from the cluttered background trays and ground tiles, making the continuous distance decrease of the approaching person on the left immediately evident. However, the depth map is unreliable across the open grid of the rack—where background depths bleed into thin metal bars to create web-like artifacts—and it flattens the distant egg trays on the ground and the green building (>15 m away) into uniform blackness.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against the unlabelled rack and outdoor yard, detecting nothing in frame 1, the wearer's extended left arm in the lower foreground (0.3–0.5 m away) and the standing person in black 2–2.5 m ahead on the upper left in frame 2, and that same person approaching to ~1 m on the far left of frames 3 and 4 while partly cut off by the left frame boundary. In frame 4, it also segments a tiny patch of the crouching person in red ~3 m away behind the rack (about 1.5–2 m behind the person on the left and largely occluded by the rack's metal bars and blue trays), and in frame 5 it detects the standing person in white and red ~3 m to the right of the rack as the camera wearer turns rightward. Both the wearer's hand in frames 2 and 4 and the left-side person's extended left arm in frames 2 and 3 are shown in close proximity (within arm's reach, <0.6 m) to the rack's frame and blue trays, with the standing people in frames 2 and 5 oriented roughly toward or sideways to the rack rather than looking at the camera wearer. This map highlights the tiny, heavily occluded figure crouching behind the rack in frame 4 that is visually camouflaged by the rusted grid in the RGB image. However, it is unreliable in object classification and completeness: it completely misses the metal rack, blue trays, and ground egg flats, fails to detect the occluded crouching person in frames 2 and 3, and mislabels the person's lower leg and wheel area at the bottom left of frame 3 as a 'skateboard'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks skeletal keypoints in the scene, rendering a yellow full-body skeleton for the person standing 2–2.5 m ahead to the upper left in frame 2 and a magenta 21-keypoint hand skeleton for the camera wearer's extended left hand at 0.3–0.5 m in the lower center of frames 2 and 4. In frame 2, the yellow skeleton shows the person facing mostly toward the camera wearer and slightly right toward the rack (head cropped at the top border), with their right arm hanging down on the left and their left arm raised horizontally to the right within arm's reach of the rack's upper-left corner, about 1.5–2 m above and ahead of the wearer's outstretched open palm. Across frames 2 to 4, the magenta hand skeleton shows the wearer's open palm angled upward and forward with splayed fingers within 0.2–0.3 m of the rack's side bars, disappearing in frames 1, 3, and 5 when the wearer's arm drops out of view as the camera turns. The pose map makes the exact finger articulation of the wearer's hand and the shoulder-hip orientation and raised left-arm reach of the person in frame 2 much clearer than in the dark, high-contrast RGB strip. However, it is highly unreliable whenever bodies are occluded or truncated by frame edges: it completely misses the approaching person's torso and arm at the left edge of frames 3 and 4, the crouching person occluded behind the rack in frames 2–4, and the sideways-facing person standing ~3 m away on the right in frame 5.
